ratings.rationale: Field alteration is tampering of observables, yielding displacement if L3 accepts biased TDOA; analogue false-data-injection evidence supports only low reproducibility; strong-pass checks detect single-satellite bias, weak-pass stealth window hides it.
ratings.issue: Delay/field-modification overlap with T2.03; no explicit multi-report consistency treatment.

ratings.rationale: Impersonated relay reports are spoofing and can create ghost tracks or corrupt real ones; satellite-downlink evidence is analogue only; L3 consistency may catch it in strong geometry but not inside weak-pass stealth.
ratings.issue: Overlaps T2.09 downlink injection; asset may also include A2.4.

ratings.rationale: Selective delay/reorder is scored as tampering because it distorts report timing; PTP/NTP delay evidence is analogue; strong-pass checks may catch bias, weak-pass stealth hides it.
ratings.issue: Transit delay does not alter embedded TOA; TDOA-distortion claim is weak and overlaps T2.01/T2.04.

ratings.rationale: Selective report loss is an enabler that raises HDOP and widens the stealth margin; LEO network DoS evidence is analogue only; L3 geometry/integrity may notice degraded HDOP but not attribute it.
ratings.issue: Authors call it a threat but it is an enabler; no direct L4 consequence.

ratings.rationale: No published mechanism for MLAT ISL crosslink denial; direct DoS could degrade one footprint; link monitoring at L2 should detect outage, lowering discoverability risk.
ratings.issue: No cited source; mechanism generic and may overlap T2.04/T2.12.

ratings.rationale: One-way PTP delay shifts clock offset without forgery, so authentication-invariant tau; clock bias maps to range bias and displacement; strong-pass checks catch, weak-pass stealth hides.
Forged/replayed PTP is spoofing of time transfer; authentication would stop it, so not primary tau; clock offset yields displacement, with strong/weak discoverability as above.
ratings.issue: Overlaps T2.06 in effect; relies on absent or weak PTP authentication.

ratings.rationale: Passive downlink/backhaul interception is disclosure only, an enabler for later injection; satellite eavesdropping evidence is analogue; consumer-grade receiver gives high exploitability but no direct ATM damage.
ratings.issue: Tier T1c conflicts with AC5 range; disclosure-only threat may be better classed as enabler.

ratings.rationale: Overshadowed downlink injection is spoofing/tampering accepted as reports, enabling ghost tracks; satellite downlink evidence is analogue; high tier needed and L3 cross-check may catch in strong geometry.
ratings.issue: Overlaps T2.02; requires downlink overshadowing not demonstrated for this constellation.

ratings.rationale: Passive command-channel capture is disclosure only, informing forgery; Iridium/SATCOM evidence is analogue; low-cost receiver gives high exploitability, and no direct ATM damage.
ratings.issue: Disclosure-only; enabler-like but scored D=1; tier/class mismatch again.

ratings.rationale: Forged commands/updates gain command path, so elevation primary with spoofing secondary; on-orbit hacking evidence is analogue; state-level access needed; effects can reach displacement/denial with late detection.
ratings.issue: Consequence class unspecified; depends on key disclosure or weak auth external to this record.

ratings.rationale: Compromised routers/terminals are an enabler for later tampering/dropping; SATCOM advisory evidence is analogue; remote exploitation is T2, and network monitoring may eventually detect.
ratings.issue: Asset register lacks explicit router/gateway asset; A2.4 is coarse.

missing_threats.why: Governance channel C can suppress or widen flags.

missing_threats.why: Consequence at ATM is not covered by L2 records.

rubric_ambiguities: Enabler versus disclosure-only scoring: D=1 versus null and goals [] are not fully exclusive.
Adversary class tiers conflict with low-cost passive interception (AC5 T2-T3 versus T1c).
Di for denial/enabler threats when checks are partial or span multiple layers.
Delay in transit versus embedded TOA: rubric lacks a test for transport delay not altering timestamps.
Evidence-level mapping and analogue subtraction are subjective for satellite-network analogues.
batch_comments.overall: The batch is mostly valid L2 threats, but several overlap (T2.02/T2.09, T2.06/T2.07, T2.01/T2.03). T2.04 and T2.12 are enablers, T2.08/T2.10 disclosure-only, and T2.05 lacks published support. Timing and report-integrity threats are the most consequential; evidence is largely analogue.
